description: OpenClaw: Gateway /tools/invoke tool escalation + ACP permission auto-approval
how_introduced: Yes. AI-authored commit 749e28dec796f77697398acbfc7a64d4439d7cad reimplemented ACP permission handling with a name-based dangerous-tool check that still auto-approved all other identified tools; later fixes (bb1c3dfe1 and 153a7644e) had to tighten that logic because it remained vulnerable. The original gateway exposure and the original ACP auto-approval bug were human-authored, but AI code was part of the causal chain for the ACP portion of this CVE.

bug_commits.author: aether-ai-agent
bug_commits.message: fix(security): block dangerous tools from HTTP gateway and fix ACP auto-approval (OC-02)

agent_verdicts.reasoning: Although framed as a security fix, this AI-authored commit reimplemented ACP permission handling with `if (!DANGEROUS_ACP_TOOLS.has(toolName))` auto-approval and selected `allow_once`/fallback for every non-dangerous named tool. The later fix bb1c3dfe1 changes that exact design to require prompting for anything outside safe read/search kinds, and 153a7644e further tightens the safe-kind inference. So 749e28 is a confirmed BIC for the residual ACP auto-approval weakness, even though the older/original bug predated it.
